ambrose-joseph: Ambrose of Milan, On Joseph (De Ioseph), about AD 388
coats-joseph: George W. Coats, From Canaan to Egypt: Structural and Theological Context for the Joseph Story (1976)
diodorus-library: Diodorus of Sicily, Library of History, book 1 (first century BC)
exodus-rabbah: Exodus Rabbah (Shemot Rabbah), a midrash on Exodus compiled in the Middle Ages from older material
hoffmeier-israel: James K. Hoffmeier, Israel in Egypt: The Evidence for the Authenticity of the Exodus Tradition (1997)
humphreys-joseph: W. Lee Humphreys, Joseph and His Family: A Literary Study (1988)
joseph-aseneth: Joseph and Aseneth, a Jewish romance in Greek (written roughly 100 BC to AD 200); translated by C. Burchard in J. H. Charlesworth, ed., The Old Testament Pseudepigrapha, vol. 2 (1985)
kugel-potiphar: James L. Kugel, In Potiphar's House: The Interpretive Life of Biblical Texts (1990)
maimonides-teshuvah: Moses Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Repentance (Hilkhot Teshuvah), about 1180
mann-joseph: Thomas Mann, Joseph and His Brothers, a novel in four parts (1933–1943)
moran-shiloh: William L. Moran, "Gen 49,10 and Its Use in Ez 21,32," Biblica 39 (1958)
redford-joseph: Donald B. Redford, A Study of the Biblical Story of Joseph (Genesis 37–50), Supplements to Vetus Testamentum 20 (1970)
vonrad-joseph: Gerhard von Rad, "The Joseph Narrative and Ancient Wisdom" (1953), in The Problem of the Hexateuch and Other Essays (1966)
westenholz-qedeshah: Joan Goodnick Westenholz, "Tamar, Qĕdēšā, Qadištu, and Sacred Prostitution in Mesopotamia," Harvard Theological Review 82 (1989)
westermann-gen: Claus Westermann, Genesis 37–50: A Commentary, translated by John J. Scullion (1986)
wevers-lxxgen: John William Wevers, Notes on the Greek Text of Genesis (1993)
wildavsky-joseph: Aaron Wildavsky, Assimilation versus Separation: Joseph the Administrator and the Politics of Religion in Biblical Israel (1993)
wise-dss: Michael Wise, Martin Abegg Jr. and Edward Cook, The Dead Sea Scrolls: A New Translation (1996; rev. ed. 2005)
maimonides-melakhim: Moses Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Kings and Their Wars (Hilkhot Melakhim), chapters 11–12 on the Messiah (about 1180)
nachmanides-barcelona: Nachmanides (Ramban), Vikuach, his own account of the Barcelona Disputation of 1263; English in Charles B. Chavel, Ramban: Writings and Discourses (1978)
tanhuma: Midrash Tanhuma, a rabbinic homiletic midrash on the Torah (compiled about AD 500–800)
ecclesiastes-rabbah: Ecclesiastes Rabbah (Kohelet Rabbah), a rabbinic midrash on Ecclesiastes (compiled about AD 600–800)
fishbane-interp: Michael Fishbane, Biblical Interpretation in Ancient Israel (1985)
goppelt-typos: Leonhard Goppelt, Typos: The Typological Interpretation of the Old Testament in the New (German 1939; English 1982)
westermann-essays: Claus Westermann, ed., Essays on Old Testament Hermeneutics (1963), with Gerhard von Rad's and Walther Eichrodt's essays on typology
collins-scepter: John J. Collins, The Scepter and the Star: Messianism in Light of the Dead Sea Scrolls (1995; 2nd ed. 2010)
rashi-isaiah: Rashi (Rabbi Shlomo Yitzchaki), commentary on Isaiah (11th century)
testaments-twelve: Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs (second century BC to second century AD); H. W. Hollander and M. de Jonge, The Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs: A Commentary (1985)
philo-joseph: Philo of Alexandria, On Joseph (De Iosepho, first century AD)
philo-migration: Philo of Alexandria, On the Migration of Abraham (De Migratione Abrahami, first century AD)
bauckham-hades: Richard Bauckham, The Fate of the Dead: Studies on the Jewish and Christian Apocalypses (1998)
